No runtime card-name switch; converter matches exact reviewed full card text and ITEM category and emits only the audited canonical identity. No second Tome as an activation discard cost. strictEffect: PokemonDiscardReplacement helper accepts only replace_basic_from_discard, CHOSEN_POKEMON and the exact declared fields/values above. Source is intrinsically actor DISCARD. No source/to/bind/as_cost or nested effects are accepted.

Runtime requires current effective field Basic and own controller even if a forged broader select scope were supplied. Attacks, Abilities, passive/automatic programs and standalone zone-selection APIs must reject the operation.

Incoming discard card must be printed POKEMON, printed Basic, supported and have an audited Pokemon profile with placement rule permitting this replacement. A discarded Fossil Item is not a Pokemon candidate. An in-play Fossil Item is an effective Basic Pokemon and can be the outgoing host; its actual physical Item card is discarded normally.
Add permitsDiscardReplacement to PokemonPlacementRule (ANY_EFFECT only), preserving existing deck/Bench methods. No new placement-rule bypass is implied.

pairedStateMachine: READY: authenticate seat/turn and require no previous pending resolution; snapshot exactly 2 distinct physical IDs located in actor hand. Reject 0/1/3, duplicates, foreign-zone IDs, stale cards, wrong group/profile, unsupported cards and locks before any mutation or RNG.

PREFLIGHT: create one representative Trainer origin and one context whose resolving Trainer set contains BOTH IDs. Existing context hand-size, hand-effect candidates and activation-cost candidate projections exclude the whole set before removal; nested contexts retain the set. Run ordinary Trainer program schema, capability, affordability and EffectPotential checks once for the logical play. No effect if there is no selectable own Basic or no eligible discard Basic; protected hosts cannot provide false positive potential.

ATTEMPT: after full validation, run the player's Trainer-attempt gate exactly once for the pair. Reuse ordinary single-card implementation through a list-aware helper, keeping its RNG label/order stable for singletons. Tails moves BOTH selected physical cards directly to their actual owners' discard; no effect cursor, history, completed event or cost. Heads proceeds without a second gate.

COMMIT: remove BOTH physical cards from hand together after validation, create one PendingResolution with immutable playedCards plus the existing representative card/category/cursor. No second pending play and no secondary discard cost. Their temporary zone is resolution, not hand/discard.

PAUSE: existing target and card transactions own authorization, revision, selection cardinality and retry semantics. Invalid target/card submissions do not move anything, reroll the attempt, discard either source, reset the cursor or release the already declared play. Reconnection resumes the same pending action. There is no post-declaration cancel/refund.

COMPLETE: after the one program finishes, move both played cards to actual-owner discard once; write both definition IDs to the turn history presence Set and capture one logical ITEM completion event batch, visiting each eligible listener once. Then use the ordinary whole-effect checkpoint for reactions, attachment correction and KOs.
A before-declaration UI cancel is purely local and consumes nothing. A newer server revision invalidates every old pair option and clears client popup/drag state.

FINISH/CONCESSION: any pending playedCards are each moved exactly once to actual owner discard; clearing pending resolution must not emit successful completion history/events. Covers both target and discard prompts and either conceding player.

eventAndHistoryContract.physicalCards: Both are played: actual printed text says to play 2 cards at once. Both physical cards are kept in the resolution payload and both definition IDs are added to handPlays upon successful completion.
eventAndHistoryContract.history: Existing handPlays is LinkedHashSet<String>, used only by CARD_PLAYED_THIS_TURN presence checks. It has no physical-card or play-count arithmetic. The pair does not create a new inferred numerical rule; two copies of the same definition naturally occupy one Set entry.
eventAndHistoryContract.completion: Root-approved engine contract: one simultaneous use is one ITEM completion envelope and one trigger batch. Current CardPlayedTriggerPolicy observes only public category/subcategory, not physical card counts or hidden IDs, so a representative identical ITEM classification is sufficient while all cards are retained in the payload/history.
eventAndHistoryContract.evidenceLimit: The six actual Tome FAQs directly confirm one attempt coin and its printed text confirms one effect. They do not separately rule on every possible future count-based Trainer-use listener. One completion envelope is the explicit implementation contract, not an invented seventh official FAQ. A future physical-card-count policy needs its own audited contract.

clientAndNetwork.entry: MatchSession generates pair actions before ordinary hand Trainer actions, in stable private-hand order i<j. Only one action per unordered pair, so four copies yield six actions. Both handKey anchors are included. Ordinary singlecard action generation skips paired profiles.
clientAndNetwork.label: Use existing prefix: 使用：变化之书 ×2（手牌第i、j张）. Ordinals refer to the current recipient-visible hand order, distinguishing copies without exposing opaque IDs in text or silently selecting an arbitrary second card.
clientAndNetwork.existingUI: MatchActionMatcher.forCards uses containsAll; either card finds its pairs. MatchTableScreen.mayStartDrag accepts either hand anchor. canTarget highlights the matching second hand card, and dropping onto it selects the one exact pair. Clicking a hand card or dragging to arena (使用： prefix) lists all matching pairs when more than one exists. MatchRegionScreen/MatchCardActionScreen already list the same server options.
clientAndNetwork.cancelAndStale: Before submit, popup Cancel/outside click and invalid drop are local only. MatchTableScreen.update clears popup/drag on any snapshot; MatchCardActionScreen.update returns to the rebuilt parent. Existing submit(connection,seat,revision,option) authenticates the actual controller, rejects stale revisions and regenerates authoritative current actions. No custom pair IDs are accepted from the client and no new command protocol is introduced.
clientAndNetwork.display: Append public List<CardInstance> resolvingTrainerCards to MatchClientView, retaining resolvingTrainer as the representative compatibility field and preserving existing constructors. Ordinary pending Trainers expose a singleton, pair exposes two, stadium activation retains its existing source behavior. Both cards are already publicly played. MatchSession adds both names; MatchRegionModel renders all played cards in the existing resolving zone. Do not expose unplayed hand identities. Snapshot transport remains the existing DTO/JSON path; no new IntentPayload.
clientAndNetwork.verification: Session integration plus MatchActionMatcher and MatchRegionModel tests must prove both anchors, pair uniqueness/ordinals, target matching from either card, spectator/foreign-seat denial, revision replay denial, both public resolving faces, and no hidden hand IDs leaked. No claim of live Minecraft UI rendering from component tests; root performs normal build/client checks.

replacementTransaction: Potential and host choice use the selected context, public own field Basic status and actual public discard candidates. The outgoing host need not have spare HP and may be Active or Bench, including rule-box Basics. Lower incoming HP can be immediately lethal and is still legal.

At opening the discard prompt, capture selected logical Pokemon ID, owner, entrySequence and physical topCardId in PokemonReplacementSource. Revalidate all four plus effective Basic state, source card still in actor discard, printed incoming Basic/profile/placement rule, physical uniqueness and effect protection before movement.

Validate ability-definition transition authorization before mutation, then call existing BattlefieldState.replaceTopCardByEffect. Remove incoming physical card from discard and put outgoing top physical card in its actual owner's discard exactly once. No shuffle or reveal acknowledgement is needed: discard is already public.

Keep logical Pokemon ID, entrySequence, enteredTurn/lastEvolvedTurn, lower stack if present, attachment physical cards/owners/entry lifetimes, damage, Special Conditions, weakness override, ordinary continuous effects, delayed marker identity, damage/heal history and Ability usage. Do not perform remove+reenter, evolve/devolve, attachment reattachment or counter-movement operations.

The host remains the same in-play Pokemon. No ON_ENTER_PLAY, ON_EVOLVE, ON_LEAVE_PLAY or energy-attachment event arises from the replacement. Current passive facts and HP/Tool capacity recompute from the incoming profile; existing settleHitPointChanges handles invalid inherited attachments and overflow prompts. KO remains deferred until the entire paired card effect has completed, and prizes use the incoming profile.

Patrat's counter-movement prohibition cannot prevent inherited damage because no counters are moved between Pokemon. Preserve old attack/received-damage history rather than rewriting the prior attacker species to the incoming species.

Physical-card-bound protection is an intentional exception: keep existing replaceTopCardByEffect pruning of cardBoundEffects tied to outgoing physical top. Ordinary equal protection remains independently inherited. Do not remap the physical token to the incoming card or change deck replacement semantics.

abilityIdentityAudit.sameAndDifferent: Keep existing per-incarnation Ability ID usage. Same Ability remains used; genuinely different unused Ability can be used. Shared player-level usage stays intact. Do not reset usage on replacement or speculate about evolution/devolution resets.
abilityIdentityAudit.definitionAuthorization: Reuse the existing server-owned validateDefinitionReplacement/authorizeDefinitionReplacement path for overlapping composed Ability IDs. Factor only if needed for deck/discard reuse without weakening arbitrary-program rejection. Test same ID with the same program and changed audited program, and A→B→A preserving prior usage. Existing dispatcher recognizes prior known programs on return.
abilityIdentityAudit.inventoryLimit: A focused current-production supported Basic manual-Ability scan found no ID crossing legacy opcode and composed adapters; effects vs triggers are both composed and must not be mistaken for separate adapters. No new generic cross-adapter usage semantics is needed for this batch. If implementation tests reveal a legal existing same-ID gap, report it before broadening the design.
abilityIdentityAudit.unsupportedFAQActors: Erika's Tangela and Larry's Komala are currently unsupported; use clearly synthetic same/different Ability fixtures for those mechanisms, without enabling the actual cards.
